source_review.notes: Reviewed current LevelDB table-format documentation and format source, current RocksDB block-based-format and table-option source plus maintainer restart-index note, Google's primary Bigtable paper, and current Cassandra SSTable architecture/tools documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Concrete layouts and versions remain scoped to their implementations.

evidence: Checked internal entry tuple, comparator, data-block interval, handle, restart interval/positions, block count, and encoded file-size notation.
Checked user key, sequence, kind, payload, separator, fence, file identity, format, and checksum context are distinct.
Checked requests, encoded/compressed/decoded/cache/index/filter/returned bytes are separate metrics.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The complexity statement is explicitly conditional on the concrete index/restart search implementation.

evidence: Recomputed shared prefixes 0,4,2,0,3,4,0 for the seven model keys and restarts 0,3,6.
Recomputed three-entry block ranges apple..apricot, banana..bandana, carrot..carrot and separators banana,carrot.
Recomputed Exercise 2 shared prefixes 0,3,0,0,0,4,0 and inclusive range anteater through bandit.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Restart entry indexes in the model are not durable byte offsets.

evidence: Verified prefix decoding by predecessor prefix plus suffix reconstructs the original key when shared length is valid.
Verified restart records bound dependency chains and a two-stage separator/restart search reaches the first key not less than target.
Verified full next-block first keys are safe right-lower-bound separators under the model's bytewise unique-key comparator.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Shortened separators and custom collations retain comparator-specific proof obligations.

evidence: Reviewed empty/single blocks, every restart/block boundary, maximum keys/values, duplicates/internal versions, reverse iteration, separators, and footer discovery.
Reviewed malformed/noncanonical varints, shared overflow, bad restart counts/offsets, wrapping handles, overlapping regions, truncation, wrong type/version/magic/comparator, and decompression bombs.

Reviewed checksum/auth failure, misplaced blocks, cache identity reuse, partial build, sync/manifest crash, stale readers, backup/replica pinning, migration/downgrade, scrub, repair, and salvage gaps.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The model excludes binary bytes, values/versions, files, checksums, corruption, publication, and concurrent lifetimes.

evidence: Encoding forces zero shared length at each restart and otherwise computes exact predecessor common prefix.
Decoding reconstructs the complete list; blocks partition that list; separators equal first keys after the first block.
Exact outputs validate restart/shared arrays, decoded order, block/index routing, two seek blocks, bounded range, round trip, and uniqueness/order.
invariant_checking.notes: The model's list boundaries are a logical analogue only; the chapter separately requires byte-record boundary validation.

evidence: Reviewed block proof from ordered inputs through canonical prefix encoding, restart validation, exact reconstruction, ordering, and contextual checksum rejection.
Reviewed routing/iteration proof from contiguous block partition and legal separators through checked handles, point seek, and endpoint-correct ranges.
Reviewed publication/lifetime proof from private file finalization/reopen/sync through manifest install, pinned versions, delayed deletion, and crash reconciliation.
proof_review.notes: These are format and lifecycle obligations, not a verified binary implementation.

evidence: Block, routing/iteration, and publication/lifetime structures are separately labeled.
Checksum, filter, footer magic, source reachability, finite round trip, and repair output keep their exact evidence scope.
Comparator compatibility, immutable lifetime, physical I/O, and production performance are never inferred from logical sorting alone.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Corruption, unsupported format, unavailable key/I/O, resource limit, absence, and deletion are explicit distinct outcomes.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact thirteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It reproduced exact prefixes/restarts, full round trip, three blocks, two separators, present/absent routing, four-entry range, and order_valid=True.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local structure/link checks passed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No binary encoder/parser, file I/O, compression, checksum, filter, cache, manifest, crash recovery, fuzz campaign, compatibility run, repair, or performance experiment was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter refines an immutable sorted sequence into a complete file protocol with internal order, bounded prefix reconstruction, block routing, authenticated metadata, failure taxonomy, publication, pinned lifetime, and evolution.

pedagogical_review.notes: The compact model makes prefix/restart/block/index behavior inspectable; ten examples cover parser, routing, compression, checksum, publication, lifetime, and tuning; five exercises provide exact computation plus complete format and incident audits.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/maintainer-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Google, LevelDB, RocksDB, Bigtable, Cassandra, database, storage-engine, binary-format, security, reliability, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed.
